_comment: BAND-SPLIT-2. This band's own dialogue container. Same `{"conversations": {...}}` shape as opening.json/village.json/trainers.json/relay.json/stronghold.json/meadows_freed.json, merged onto the same table by scripts/story/dialogue_runner.gd::table() (EXTRA_DIALOGUE_PATHS). Unlike the four content configs BAND-SPLIT cut, this is a dictionary keyed by conversation id, not a positional array -- there is no `order` to preserve, because lookup is always by id and never by position. A trainer or NPC placed in band1_lower_meadows gets its dialogue written here instead of appended to trainers.json, so a band author never has to touch a file another band is also writing to.
_comment_tournament_1: TOURNAMENT-1 / FIRST-HOUR-FUN-REBUILD. The village tournament's whole script, plus the South Bridge gatekeeper's. Halda is the marshal (data/config/village_npcs.json); her ordered `greeting_when` list uses existing progression flags, not a tournament state machine. Her first registration conversation sets `opening:tournament_registered` and names the complete-team, camp, Creature Bed, rest/recovery and strength requirements. The three round conversations end on `battle:<trainer_id>` and are spoken by the OPPONENT rather than by Halda, because the fight starts the frame that box closes and the last voice the player hears should be the person about to send a creature out.
_comment_saddle: `tournament_halda_champion` is the NPC line the owner directive asks for: it says out loud that a Meadowhart can be ridden, and that the saddle needs rootstone from past the crossing. It does NOT carry a `flag:` effect -- the saddle pattern is granted by `tournament_final_oskar`'s own `reward.flags` the moment the final is won, so a player who never walks back to Halda still has it. The line explains the prize; it is not the prize. That split is deliberate: a reward that can only be collected by re-reading a conversation is a reward that gets lost.
_comment_portraits: Every conversation here uses the trainer portrait plate, the only villager portrait on disk (assets/ui/portraits/ holds grandpa.png and trainer.png and nothing else). tests/test_dialogue_runner.gd::test_every_conversation_has_a_speaker_and_a_portrait_that_is_really_there requires a real file, and CLAUDE.md's prototyping rule allows the stand-in. The grunt in particular should get a faction plate when Team Tether has portrait art of its own.

tournament_halda.speaker: Halda
lines: Halda. I keep the board up there and I keep the draw honest, which in this village is two jobs.
Eight slots, four bouts, then two, then one. Same as it's been run since before the road went quiet.

tournament_halda_closed.speaker: Halda
lines: You'll want the tournament, then. Everyone does, first week.
Rule's the rule: I don't put a name on that board unless there's a proper team stood behind it. One creature isn't a team, it's a favourite.
Fill out all five places. Then we can talk about whether they're ready.

tournament_halda_register.speaker: Halda
lines: You want your name on the board? Good. Here is what I need to see before I take it.
Five creatures. Not borrowed bodies -- your whole team. Train them until they can stand in the ring.

lines.text: Make a real camp: tent, fire and your bedroll. Build a Creature Bed, let one of them recover there, then come back with everyone rested, fed and happy.

lines: No walls or fancy workshop required. I need proof you can keep a team, not a house.

tournament_halda_train.speaker: Halda
lines: All five of them. Good. Now look at them.
Half of that lot have never taken a real hit. I'd be signing them up for a hiding, and I'd be the one who did it.
Take them out. Fight things. Feed them, rest them, let them grow into it. Then we'll talk about the board.

tournament_halda_condition.speaker: Halda
tournament_halda_condition._comment: RG19-spec/D68. The entry gate the owner named in his own words: 'They have to be well rested, well fed, and happy.' Shown when the team is big enough and levelled enough but not in shape. Deliberately written as a reason and a to-do list, not a refusal -- she names the three things and where to go and do them, and the team screen's own condition line says WHICH creature is short of WHICH. The thresholds are in data/config/creature_condition.json and are not repeated here or anywhere else.
lines: Levels aren't the whole of it. Look at the state of them.

That one's dead on its feet, and that one hasn't eaten since you found it. I've seen tired creatures put in front of a crowd before. It doesn't go well for them and it doesn't go well for the person who entered them.
Beds at home, a proper feed, and time out with you where nothing's trying to bite them. Berries do fine. Then come back and I'll put your name up.

tournament_halda_camp.speaker: Halda
lines: They look strong enough. Now show me they have somewhere safe to come back to.
I want a proper camp, a Creature Bed, and one real night of recovery there. A team that can fight is not yet a team you can keep.

tournament_halda_signup.speaker: Halda
lines: Now that's a team. Look at them stood there like they've done this before.

lines.text: Right. Slot one, and I've drawn you Mira in the first bout — she'll not go easy on you because she sold you a potion. Board's up behind me; the other half of the draw fills in as it's fought.

tournament_halda_champion.speaker: Halda
lines: Champion of the Lower Meadows. I'll want that written on the board properly, not in my hand.
Here — the pattern for a riding saddle. It's Oskar's, by rights; he said give it to whoever took the Meadowhart off him.
A Meadowhart will carry you once you've built one. Rootstone for the frame, and the only rootstone left is past the south crossing. So: earn it, then go and get it.

tournament_quarter.speaker: Mira
lines: First bout, then. Don't look at me like that — the meadow doesn't care who's nice to it either.

lines.text: Whole team out this time. Nothing held back, same as I promised you in the square.

tournament_quarter_beaten.speaker: Mira
lines: Out in the first. Well. Somebody's got to be, and I'd rather it was to you.

tournament_semi.speaker: Tam
lines: Semi-final. Fen put up more than the board says, mind — I've a limp to prove it.

lines.text: You know my lesson. Let's see whether you learned it or just heard it.

tournament_semi_beaten.speaker: Tam
lines: Switched on me twice and I never saw the second one coming. That's the lesson, that is.

tournament_final.speaker: Oskar
lines: Final. Bryn took me to the last creature in the semi and I'm still short of breath.
You'll not have seen this one out on the road. She's not a fighter by trade — she's a road, if you know how to sit on her.

lines.text: Beat her and the pattern's yours. Halda holds it. Come on.

tournament_final_beaten.speaker: Oskar
lines: Took the Meadowhart off me fair. Go and see Halda — the pattern's hers to hand over, and I'll not go back on it.

south_bridge_grunt_challenge.speaker: Tether Grunt
lines: Far side's closed. Company business. Go back up the road.
No, I don't know what's over there either. I know what I'm paid to stand in front of.
Two of mine, nothing special. If that string at your heel is worth anything at all, this won't take long.

lines.text: You're not walking round me and you're not talking round me. Fine. Beat me and the key's yours; that's not company policy, that's mine.

south_bridge_grunt_beaten.speaker: Tether Grunt
lines: Take it. I'll tell them you had a key already.
Straight over and don't stop on the span. There's nothing down there but the old road.

old_champion_challenge.speaker: Old Bram
old_champion_challenge._comment: Prompt 30's Old Champion: 'character/trainer history and a memorable battle or lesson using an existing NPC rig/team'. The history is Team Tether's arrival told from the losing side, which is the same story the site front door tells and the same one Grandpa is too old to finish -- so this is canon being said by somebody else, not a new thread. He never asks the player for anything and sets no flag until he is beaten: prompt 30 forbids the fetch-quest template and this is the opposite of one.
lines: Sit if you like. I've not got anywhere to be.
You'll be the one they're all talking about. Won the ribbon down in the square.

lines.text: I won it too. Long time ago now. Held it eleven years.

lines: Then the Tether came up the road with their pylons and their paperwork, and I went down to the bridge to tell them no.
I was fifty-three and I had two creatures who'd never lost. Neither of those facts helped.

lines.text: So. You're going that way, and I'd like to know whether it's worth me hoping. Show me.

old_champion_beaten.speaker: Old Bram
old_champion_beaten._comment: The payoff line. The items and coins are granted by the trainer's own `reward` block the moment the fight is won (data/config/bands/band1_lower_meadows/trainers.json), so a player who walks off and never speaks to him again keeps them -- this is the acknowledgement, not the delivery. The last two lines are the ONLY place the elder mosshell (spawns.json order 1900) is named anywhere in the game. Prompt 30: some optional content should be found by curiosity, and secrets should not be pre-labelled on the map, so the elder has no marker -- but a player who did the harder optional thing gets told where the other one is, which makes the two a chain instead of two icons.
lines: Ha. Well.
That's the first time in nine years I've enjoyed losing.
Take the orbs. I've no use for them and you're going to need them -- the far side of that bridge doesn't hand anything over.
One more thing, since you've earned the telling.
West of the pond, past where the path bends away, there's a hollow that stays green when everything round it burns off. There's a mosshell down there older than I am.
I've never been able to take it. You might. Mind it sees you coming a long way off.
